annotations.title: Draft a rikma from a blueprint

description:
Turn a business, an existing partnership or an idea into a draft rikma on 1lev1: the rikma, its PRODUCTS, missions, resources and partners. Use it when someone wants to add their business so the concierge can find and order from them, to see how their partnership would look on 1lev1, or to break an idea down and recruit partners. Build it yourself from the site you read or from the conversation:
- products FIRST: every distinct thing they sell is a product, with its price when it is stated (do not invent prices - leave price out and ask), and `keywords`: the words a customer would use for the need it answers, not the product name (a "brunch tray" answers "catering", "breakfast for guests"), and `categories`: 1-3 broad domains ("events", "food") - they are linked to the platform's existing categories, which the concierge compares with every wish.
- missions and resources only when they make a product (put their refs in the product recipe) or when someone is still needed. holder "me" = the person you are talking to does it; holder "open" = recruit someone; holder "partner" + partnerRef = an exact `ref` from a row in `partners`. For every partner to invite, add a partner row with a user-provided email and link each mission/resource they will bring with holder "partner" and partnerRef. Do not invent or infer an email; ask the person for it. A partner row without an email cannot receive email, and a partner without linked missions/resources gets only the general rikma join invitation.
- a running cost is priced per period, never as a total: rent or a subscription is a resource with kindOf "monthly" (or "yearly") and its price per month; ongoing work every month is a mission with `recurring: true` and `hours` per month.
- `why` on each row: one sentence of where it came from ("the site lists it at 180").
Pass projectId to add to a rikma the person is already a member of. The draft is the user's own; a rikma prepared for another person is prepareForSomeoneElse. Show the rows to the person in the conversation, ask about anything you guessed (prices especially), and confirm every partner email before using it - never invent an address. To invite a partner to contribute, add them in partners with a ref, then set holder:"partner" and partnerRef to that exact ref on each mission/resource they will bring; listing a partner alone does not create a work invitation. Fix what they say with setAssistantItems, then give them reviewUrl: on that page they tick what to create and create it with one click. On creation the server sends a partner invitation email when delivery is allowed; registered partners also get mission/resource invitation cards. The result reports delivery and includes a join link to share if no email could be sent. Nothing exists and no invitation is sent until the person creates it there. Docs: https://1lev1.com/mcp#proposeRikmaBlueprintTool

holder.description: me = the person importing does it; open = recruit someone; partner = link to a partner by partnerRef and invite them to contribute.

hours.description: Hours in total, or per month when recurring

partnerRef.description: Exact `ref` of the partner who will do this mission when holder is "partner".

email.description: Email address to send the rikma invitation to. Ask the person for it; never guess or invent it. If omitted, no email invitation can be sent.

projectId.description: An existing rikma of the caller to import into (from findUserProjectsTool).

holder.description: me = the person importing does it; open = recruit someone; partner = link to a partner by partnerRef and invite them to contribute.

kindOf.description: monthly / yearly = a running cost (rent, subscription); price is then per month / year

partnerRef.description: Exact `ref` of the partner who will provide this resource when holder is "partner".

price.description: Per month / year when kindOf is monthly / yearly, otherwise the whole price

sourceText.description: The site text or conversation summary this was drawn from.
